utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'd first like to move into private session, because, Mr. Jordash, the matter you want to raise is related to testimony to be given in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought in, it's -- we just received information from VWS of a nature that would properly be considered disclosable under Rule 68 with respect to this witness that's currently on the stand. We have just sent it to both Defence teams, so I just notify them that they should check their e-mail prior to proceeding with the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, for Rule 68, one would check its e-mail, isn't it. Is it Rule 68(A) or (B) or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd have to check. It's exculpatory information, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because Rule 68 covers more ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Maksic. I'd like to remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. I invite you to be seated, and Mr. Bakrac will cross-examine you. Mr. Bakrac is counsel for Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you to Mr. Groome. We have checked the e-mail. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Good afternoon, Mr. Maksic.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, yesterday you said that you were on the command for the defence of the city of Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was serving there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you recall what was the military post of the Bubanj Potok barracks or training grounds?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are asking you this in relation to some other witnesses, so we just wanted to seize the opportunity that you were there.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the command of the city had over 25 units and military posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. You can't remember and that's all very well. You said yesterday in your evidence that the leaders and volunteers of Seselj and Serbian Renewal Movement were given equipment and weapons from the Belgrade Corps. Do you know where they were given the assets?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Bubanj Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you said, Mr. Maksic, that at some point you took along a group of individuals and met up with Mr. Biorcevic at Bogojevo. You said that it was Bogojevo training grounds or Erdut training grounds. Was it really the training grounds there?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said Bogojevo because I could not recall at that moment what the training grounds close to Bogojevo were called. I recalled later on that the name was Erdut. This was the training grounds for the units from the Osijek Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, let -- let's make it quite clear. When you said -- say Osijek Division, this means, in other words, that the training grounds belonged to the Yugoslav People's Army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksic. I will now move on to a different topic. Yesterday you testified about two situations where, in your view, Mr. Simatovic, or rather you refer to him as Frenki, on two occasions where Mr. Simatovic was in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't want to call in question the good intentions you have to testify and tell the truth here. However, especially when it comes to nicknames and some other circumstances, we can have cases of mistaken identity involved. Let me ask you this: I spoke to my client, and during the time period you claim to have seen him in Knin or Korenica, he maintains that he was not in the area of Krajina at all. This is my question for you: Did you yourself see the individual you were told was Frenki, or did you only hear that Frenki was present there?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I saw it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On both occasions you yourself saw the individual you were told was Frenki?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have full respect for your age and I know that the lapse of time is lengthy, but can you please describe for us what the individual you told was Frenki looked like?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's taller than me by a head, and he wore glasses, and that's the extent of the description I can give.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he have short or long hair?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't recall the details. I did not study him. I only cast a glance at him. I said yesterday that I had never heard the name before, so when I heard it then it meant nothing to me. Later on they explained to me that he came from the State Security Service. I said, and I'm repeating my words, I don't care about Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I understand. The only thing you recall is that he was taller than you and that he wore glasses.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And nothing else. What sort of hairstyle he had?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just looked at him and it didn't matter to me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he wear civilian clothes or uniform?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that either. I think he wore civilian clothes, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Maksic, let's move on. Mr. Maksic, yesterday you corrected your testimony from an earlier trial where you discussed a military operation in Gospic or in its surroundings.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't in Gospic proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that the 9th Corps was the unit charged with the operation, which led the operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if that was the responsible unit. According to our rules and instructions, the unit which is the highest in structure and its commander would be in charge of an operation. Since the units of the 9th Corps, complete with nine tanks, and this is hearsay now, took part in the operation, and it wasn't an operation, it was an attack on Gospic, I suppose that the commander in charge of the attack was the commanding officer of the 9th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, according to the rules of combat and based on what you just told us, people who came from the Serbian Renewal Movement, Arkan's men, and Giska's men had to be under the control and command of the commander of the 9th Corps.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They should have but they were not. They were in co-ordinated action with the 9th Corps. They were not subordinated to them. Let me explain what the difference between subordination and co-ordinated action is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, I don't have time for theories. Don't hold this against me.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'll put my next question to you, but be patient and please make a pause so that the interpreters can interpret what we say properly. So when you say "co-ordinated action," this other group also had to have had a commander who co-operated with the commander of the 9th Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the commander who attacked Gospic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: They had to co-ordinate their action.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: They had to plan the operation, the action, together and everything else?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, you said that the units -- or, rather, the volunteers of Vojislav Seselj, the Serbian Radical Party, were under the command of the army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a unit in the 9th Corps, in the 180th Brigade in Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic were the volunteered of the SBO, the Serbian National Guard, that's to say, of the Serbian Renewal Movement, were they also under the command of the army?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would I like to call in e-court 2D161, and I would like Mr. Maksic to have a look at it. Before it appears on our screens, Your Honours, I discussed these documents with my learned friend Mr. Farr yesterday. This is a documentation that the Defence obtained from a book entitled "Domominski [phoen] Rat," "Homeland War," and all these documents can be found in that. The Defence asked for originals of these documents from the Croatian authorities, and since we will be calling witnesses who would be able to testify to these documents, we shall be using documents from the book, and with your leave we understand that Mr. Farr and the OTP don't object. We would like to use this documentation and we would like the documentation to be MFI'd until such time as we receive the originals of these documents from Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: It's correct. We're happy for these documents to be used and agree that they just be MFI'd pending --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Just one comment. There are occasions where parts of other documents are included in the document on e-court and those should possibly be redacted and a new version uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you informed -- of course the Chamber cannot take any objection not knowing what part of what documents are to be protected. May I can take it you have informed --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: It's something I just noticed this morning. It's not an urgent point, but for example with the document we're about to see now in the B/C/S version, there's -- you see the bottom of the previous document, but it's not an urgent issue for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Bakrac, you're required to pay proper attention to any part of a document which may be shown on the screen and which perhaps should not be shown on the screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will do so. I will ask my learned colleague to make note of what it is that should be MFI'd and what it is that should remain outside of the document. And the English translation only relates to the documents we call, so there is no danger, no similar danger, there. They can remain in the English version as they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So this is, Mr. Vukic --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. So this is the report from the commander of the 9th Corps of the JNA to the command -- to the Supreme Command in Belgrade, and on the 2nd of December, the commander, Lieutenant-General Vladimir Vukovic, the commander of the 9th Corps wrote the report; is that right? You have looked at it. Is the document familiar?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Maksic, take a look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 4 of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as the translation is concerned, yesterday we saw a document which also started with "druze generale," and then it was "comrade general," and today it seems to be a only a general anymore. Is that -- has the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Here in the heading we have the name -- oh, yes, Your Honour. You're right. "Comrade" is missing in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I get a bit concerned if I see that the translation is -- I don't know where it comes from, but could you take care that it will be reviewed. Now, leaving out the word "comrade" might not immediately change the content of the document but, it's -- just caught my eye. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We will bear that in mind. Can we now see page 4 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Look at the third paragraph from the top. The sentence starts with "Members of the RJ."

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you zoom in on this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you zoom in on the top part of the document, please. Your Honours, it is somewhere around the middle of the page in the English version. It says: "Members of the RJ from the territory of the SAO Krajina in the Republic of Montenegro are well motivated and they are good fighters. Volunteers of the Serbian Guard have accepted the unified insignia and are good soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this fact, which is referred to in this document here, namely that the volunteers of the Serbian Guard - and I believe those are the volunteers of the Serbian Renewal Movement - that they have accepted the uniform insignia, that they are referred to as good soldiers, good fighters, the report being by the commander of the 9th Corps, is that not a clear sign that they are within or, rather, subordinated to the 9th Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the signature on this document, please, because this is an excerpt from a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is an excerpt from a book, and the document reads, if you can see in brackets on the first page which is VR, which means by one's own hand, that is in Croatian. That means that there is a signature, a personal signature by the signatory.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this is not an original document of the kind that could have been written by the commander of the 9th Corps, General Vukovic, and I prove this by the following -- please revert to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we, Your Honours, have the first page on the screen again because it has a VR sign and MP, which is the stamp, the place for the stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is it. Thank you. First of all, this heading, where it says, commander of the 9th Corps, strictly confidential, number so-and-so, the 2nd of December, 1991, and then it goes on to say Commander Lieutenant-General Vladimir Vukovic. According to the rules of official correspondence and also according to combat rules, let me not list them all at this point, a document of this kind simply does not exist. Secondly, never does a subordinate address a superior. This document -- I don't know to whom this is actually addressed here. We don't say a report [B/C/S Spoken], but [B/C/S Spoken] report. Thirdly, what does Vukovic -- Vladimir Vukovic have to do with volunteers who are in Montenegro? He is the commander of the 9th Corps in Knin, and from Knin to Podgorica there are several hundred kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, let us not waste time. Let us not comment any more. This is a report on soldiers who happened to be with the JNA in Knin at that time and hailed from Montenegro and Macedonia; inter alia, reference is made to members of the Serbian Guard who evidently are under the command of the 9th Corps. At the end of this document there is a footnote. There is a stamp on this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I have seen, I repeat this is not a standard, an original document according to its content and according to its form.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move that this document be MFI'd until we have the document's original from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D100 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D100 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D100 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now see 2D181 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, please look at this document. This is an official note of an operative of the state security department of Korenica in the SAO of Krajina about the latest information about the activities of the Serbian Guard in our area, and the date it bears is the 23rd of October, 1991. If you take a look at this document, what it says is that the recently arrived detachment of the Serbian guard, 50-men strong, has been -- has placed themselves under the command of the Gracac OS TO, which is the municipal of the Territorial Defence, more precisely under the command of Lieutenant-Colonel Spanovic ... Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did the Territorial Defence Staff of Gracac municipality, was it under the command of Lieutenant-Colonel Spanovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember. They changed the commanders, that is, but about what you said, the volunteers would not be dispatched directly to the TO staff of Krajina but to the individual TO staffs of the different municipalities which directly communicated with men, with the people who actually gathered, armed, and equipped the volunteers. So I would be supposed to know about this but I don't know about it, and it is the 23rd of October, 1991. It is possible that 21, as you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fifty.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifty volunteers, in fact, went and placed themselves under the command of the Municipal Staff of the TO of Gracac. It is possible but I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can, Your Honours, can this document also receive an MFI number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D101, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it will keep that status for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have another document in connection with the Serbian Guard. Actually, I have a whole lot of them, but this will be sufficient because of the limited time for this witness. Can we have 2D182, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will tell you what this is about, Mr. Maksic, before it is shown on the screen. It is the report of the command of the 1st Brigade of the TO of the IKM, which is the former command post of the 9th Corps of the 12th -- of the Otisic IKM, the forward command post of the 12th of November, 1991. You can see it says on the left side command -- command 1 number TO of the SAO Krajina, at the IKM of the -- SS, I believe, stands for village of Otisic on the 12th of November, 1991, report on the engagement of a unit of the Serbian Guard. The document starts with the words "an infantry platoon, strong unit of the Serbian Guard, Vojvoda Misic was one of the units sent to assist the forces securing the axis leading to Sinj." Did you see --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I don't see who it is addressed to, this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is a report on the engagement --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But to whom is it addressed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We shall see in the second page.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we should -- that should be on the first page to the addressee. This is what it says here is the command of the 1st Brigade, and I will say a few words about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us go through the entire document. Let us now look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where it says the 13th of November, 1991, Vrlika --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see that. I have the first page on my screen which says the forward command post Otisic. I cannot see the second page. I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the 13th of November 1991 Vrlika, the commander of the -- the commander of the IKM towards Sinj, the Commander Lieutenant-Colonel Rade Rajic, et cetera. Are you familiar with the names of these officers?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajic is -- I'm familiar with Rajic. He was my superior, and he was there in the field, but I'm not familiar with this document, because this brigade was resubordinated to the 9th Corps. And I suppose that the report sent by the commander of the 1st Brigade from the first page is sending this to the commander of the 9th Corps and not to the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From the forward command post they seem to be sending it to the brigade command; right? You can see that.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say to the command of the 9th Corps the resubordination involved the 9th Brigade of the JNA. I don't know which exactly brigade of the JNA it was with the commander of the brigade being Commander Djukic. This brigade was resubordinated to the 9th Corps according to this, to this particular JNA commander. If it's not clear, I can repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us just be more specific. So you have never seen this document before, but according to the content and the signatories, you believe that --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Rajic, yes, that is for sure. The other ones -- as for the other ones, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document also be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The MFI number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now see 65 ter -- Exhibit 65 ter 352 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, we shall now move away from the SPO volunteers, and please take a look and read this brief document which is dated the 25th of November, 1991, and it is from Petrinja. Please read it. Read it to yourself so that we do not waste time, and please tell me whether you know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this which is half-typed and half-handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please have the second page. Actually, it is the second page that we are interested in B/C/S, and the English page is the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Take a look at this page, Mr. Maksic. Does the 25th of November, 1991, that is the time when you were in the area of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the Municipal Assembly of Petrinja, Dr. Radovan Maljkovic, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had this commander, Krajina was divided into areas Banja and Kordun, and our commander was Colonel Vujaklija , who regrettably is dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: According to what you know, we can see here that members of the unit of Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan were participating in fightings on JNA and Territorial Defence positions in Petrinja municipality, and that the unit would be commanded by a senior officer and would be part of and under the command of the commander of the 2nd MTB of the 622nd Motorised Brigade, Bogdan Ercegovac?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this document, and I don't see how it relates to the -- how the president of the Municipal Assembly of Petrinja had anything to do with the execution of combat actions, but he is the one who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name of Bogdan Ercegovac?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogdan?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Bogdan Ercegovac.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was the 622nd Motorised Brigade in that area?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a brigade. I don't know what its name according to establishment was. I know that the commander of this zone was Colonel Vujaklija and he was the one who sent reports to us. He didn't send us this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This has a signature and a stamp. Do you have any reason to doubt the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't doubt its authenticity. It's just that I doubt the signature. I mean for the municipality of Petrinja -- for the Petrinja municipality Assembly and signed by the president. I'm saying what -- what is the relevance? What is the connection between the president of this municipality and the execution of combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will just ask you one question and then I shall move for a break. You said that there existed municipal TO staffs.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in every municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were they commanded by the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why are you then surprised by the fact that the president of the municipality says that he will invite units of Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan to participate in fighting in positions of the JNA and TO?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that should have been done by the TO commander of that particular municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you not say a minute ago that the municipal units of Territorial Defence were commanded by the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the TO -- municipal TO commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like the supreme commander of any -- in any state actually does it through the Supreme Staff, Supreme Command Staff. And the document is original.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move that this document be admitted into the case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of my concerns is that the translation is bearing stamps of other cases, and I would like to have a clean copy for translation. You see that, Mr. Bakrac. Could you upload, not necessarily immediately, but could you upload a clean version of the -- of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a Prosecution document, but if you wish us to assist, we shall ask for a properly visible translation of the stamp which it bears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask for that. As a matter of fact. I was referring to the stamp I find at the top of the document, which is a reference to -- you see that. Exhibit Number --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: To be Exhibit D140 [sic] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's helpful information but it was not the matter I addressed. Do you see that, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, are you referring to the English version or to the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the English version. I was talking about the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "OTP reference --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move a little bit further up in the English version. Yes. You see there is a full stamp and all kind of information about the status this document had in another case. That's not what I expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that this is a number P of this exhibit from some other case. I believe it is the Milosevic case, but we can ask for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's relatively easy if you just take that part out, but I do see the other point. I noticed already that the translation doesn't say anything about a stamp being on the original at the bottom, another reason, perhaps, to review the translation and the accuracy in full of the English version. Madam Registrar, you have already assigned a number to this document which is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. It is Exhibit D103. I just see the transcript says 104, which is incorrect. It's 103, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in connection with volunteers, I only have another video-clip, so in accordance with what you instruct us, we can either go through that video-clip or take our break now and then I would be finished actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd be finished with your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I wondered what you were finished with, but let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I would have been done with this subject on volunteers, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we do that after the break. We'll first have a break and we'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Before I proceed, owing to the goodness of Mr. Laugel, the last document that we saw, D103, was replaced in the e-court and now it bears no stamp any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, I would now like to play a video-clip that is four minutes long and a couple of seconds more. This is a celebration, and I won't tell you where. I would just ask you to pay attention to the site, the place, and also the individuals that appear in the footage, and then I will have a few questions for you after the video-clip has been shown. So please pay attention to the place where this is transpiring, where this is happening, and the individuals that are shown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Our blood drenched Serbian land."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, we will pause here. The last -- or, rather, the speaker after Arkan, and we could agree that this is Arkan, could you tell us who the other speaker was?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other speaker? Well, the first one was Milan Martic, and the other one is not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The person that we see on the screens before us, you don't know him?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that this is Sejdo Bajramovic, the then member of Presidency of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that he was a member of the SFRY Presidency, but I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the location where this ceremony was held?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was, in my view, in Golubic, at the camp. This place looks like Golubic to me. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you recognise any of the military personnel there, anyone from the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could see Colonel Ratko Mladic. I recognised Hadzic, although I've never seen him in person, but I did see him appearing on television. So I recognised those four individuals, Martic, Ratko Mladic, Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, and one more person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, let me try and help you. Could you recognise Jugoslav Kostic, also a member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Jugoslav Kostic. Well, I don't know exactly what he was at the time, whether he was the president of the Presidency or a member, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Presidency of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, it was still a federal republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, it was the Federal Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, is it your intention to identify persons who we see, or is there any other matter which you would like to raise, because I take it that the presence of most of these people would be easy to -- to agree on with the Prosecution. Why should we ask a witness whether he saw Mr. Mladic or whomever if that could be easily agreed upon? So if there's any other matter that you'd like to raise, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one -- or, rather, two more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: One was could you recognise any other officials of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the footage that we've seen, did you see and recognise any official of the Republic of Serbia MUP or the Republic of Serbia State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksic. I would now like to go back -- but I see Mr. Farr is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. I just wanted to make sure that the record was clear as to what video was being shown. The ERN is V000-6733, and a portion of that from 2 minutes and 45 seconds to 4 minutes and 38 seconds has been admitted as P14, but I believe that the portion up to 2 minutes and 45 seconds is not yet in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll deal with the bookkeeping. Mr. Bakrac will have uploaded this, I take it, and will have specified it precisely. Let's not -- I'm already a bit concerned about what we did the last six or seven minutes. The only thing, the location, fine, that's what the witness told us. Everything else, it seems to me, was perfectly fit for to agree upon. Who spoke, who's there, I mean, these are not matters for which we have to spend minutes and minutes in court, do we. Please proceed, and try to get -- to elicit evidence -- to elicit evidence which assists us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, if you just allow me another moment. I was not present during the owing statement made by the Prosecution, but I did look at their pre-trial brief, and the subject matter or the gist of this -- these proceedings is the involvement of representatives of the Serbian MUP. Now, here we can see members of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Presidency who are present in Golubic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, fine, but why do we have to hear that from a witness if you could agree on that? Is there any dispute about the person shown? Is there any dispute about Mr. -- even some persons the witness doesn't know personally, Mr. Hadzic. Why spend time on that in court?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, is there any dispute about the persons shown on this video on they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I personally don't know for every single one of them, but we certainly could have agreed to most of those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's what you're expected to do. Tell the Prosecution we would like to show this. We find it's relevant for this and this person. We want the witness to tell us what the location is. Do we agree on the persons appearing. And then you sit together and you don't have to spend time on it in court. It's a waste of time, unless there's anything else you would like to ask the witness about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We will do so in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, I would like now to go back to what my learned friend Mr. Jordash asked you about, namely the plea agreement for the late Mr. Babic, paragraph 26. First of all, I would like to ask you whether it is true that sometime in the first half of 1991 Mr. Babic got in touch with you and asked you to -- and tried to persuade you to come to the Territorial Defence Staff, Krajina Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He tried to get me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the Belgrade area, could you tell us approximately how many colonels there were in the Belgrade military area?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were quite a few of them, because the command of the defence staff of the city of Belgrade was there. The chief -- the chiefs -- the military academy, the medical hospital was there. So there were a lot of colonels. I don't know exactly the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us why it was that Mr. Babic asked you personally, you particularly, and got in touch with you particularly in order to try to persuade you to come and assume that function in Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, while I was the commander of -- a regiment commander, I was in touch with a platoon commander. He was a communications platoon commander, Kalicanin, and he got in touch with Dragus who was from Krajina and who was a resident of Belgrade. I don't know what it was that they discussed, but Kalicanin probably proposed to him in view of the fact that the Belgrade Corps was --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I appreciate what you are trying to tell us about, but could you please be brief in your answers and just focus on my questions. Why did Babic ask you particularly to go there?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because in the Belgrade Corps I was considered -- not only in the Belgrade Corps but also elsewhere I was considered to be an expert on Territorial Defence because I had under my control most of the TO units from the Belgrade Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And this was sometime in June or July 1991 or before June or July?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I believe I was taken to his sister's apartment in Zemun, and we had a conversation of some hour or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We can agree, then, that paragraph 26 which you discussed with Mr. Jordash, where it says that as of July 1991 Babic as the minister of defence signed the orders to organise TO formations in Krajina and appointed its commander. In other words, what is stated there is completely in accordance with what you're saying -- what you're telling us here: As of July and June Babic had been trying to contact personnel and find the appropriate people to go to Krajina.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably so, but I don't know. He didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Babic had good connections within the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not. If you're referring to the Chief of the General Staff and his collegium, then the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I would now like you to see a Prosecution document, 65 ter 392. 65 ter 392, please. Sir, this is an order dated 8th of August, 1991. Can you recognise the stamp and signature of Dr. Milan Babic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you see that on the 8th of August, 1991, he appointed Milan Martic as the deputy commander of Territorial Defence, and then in brackets it says "(armed forces) of the Krajina SAO."

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that in keeping with what was mentioned in Article 26 of the plea agreement where Babic said that he had appointed on the 8th of August, 1991, Milan Martic as deputy commander of Territorial Defence of SAO Krajina and that at a later date he himself issued a decision whereby he appointed himself as the commander of the TO forces in SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's request: Could the counsel please read a little more slowly, and could they make pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will try to be briefer. So in the plea agreement in paragraph 26 it says that Mr. Babic, on the 1st of August, appointed himself as commander of the armed forces of Krajina SAO, including all Special Purpose Units in SAO Krajina and TO units, and that on the 8th of August, 1991, Milan Babic appointed Milan Martic as deputy commander of the TO forces. Does this document confirm that?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, there's something that is illogical here. He is the commander of the armed forces of Krajina, and then he appoints Martic as deputy commander of Territorial Defence. Now, who was the commander of the TO? So whose deputy is Milan Martic supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, that's precisely my point. Now, you who were there -- now, we see that this document is dated 8th of August. You're right there in September.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. There was no commander because why would then Djujic be sent there? Why would he go there?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you allow the possibility then that Babic himself in his plea agreement says that he was the commander of the armed forces and the TO and that on the 8th of August he appointed Martic as his deputy?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about that, and I couldn't say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D104, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we spent a couple of minutes just to establish that there is a document which confirms in paragraph 26, isn't it? Any dispute about that, Mr. Farr?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please come to ask focused questions which assist the Chamber. I mean, if that is what Mr. Babic said in his plea agreement, if there is a clear order in which he says, "I appoint Mr. Martic as deputy commander," then to ask does this confirm what is found in the plea agreement, you don't need a witness, I could tell you because this exactly says what is found in the plea agreement. If there are any issues as to who then was the commander, then focus on that instead of asking useless questions on matters which you could easily agree upon. The document says it. I mean -- Mr. Bakrac, we are here to be assisted by the evidence of witnesses, not to spend time on not receiving anything in addition to what we know already. Please proceed. Keep in mind that, as I always say, that we'll closely monitor the way in which you use your time for cross-examination, and we're for the going to grant you all the time you asked for if you proceed in this way. And that's true for the video. That's true for this document. So please get a clear focus on what you're asking the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we now please see P965. That is a document dated 18th September, 1991, sent to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia to General Colonel Simovic personally. The document was sent by Minister Milan Martic, and it is a request for ammunition and other military equipment for the needs of the TO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. What date are you referring to, the 18th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at page 1 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't want to go through all the nine pages of this document, but in essence, this is a request for ammunition and equipment for the Territorial Defences of all the various municipal TO staffs. Are you familiar with this, that municipal TO staffs in SAO Krajina were being armed by the Ministry of Defence of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were armed, but where the weapons came from, who had sent it, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. This is already in evidence as P965.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please pull up 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's P965.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, was there any dispute about the last document, that this is a request for ammunition and other armaments sent to -- and that was ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and this document was admitted yesterday, as Mr. Bakrac indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there's no dispute about the -- what it -- what it is and what it -- because the witness couldn't say anything about it. So therefore -- let's look at the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I did not know whether the witness knew anything about this document or not. That's why I was very brief in my question, and his answer was brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, before we see the next document, let me ask you this: After the Vance Plan, after the 9th Corps withdrew from Krajina, did it leave behind its weaponry and 90 per cent of its personnel?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was not in Krajina at the time, but I know that it did leave behind some of its weaponry, not all of it, and since the 9th Corps was made up of mostly Krajina personnel, about 60 per cent of its personnel was from Krajina, they just stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we now please see 65 ter 412.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Farr showed you this document, Witness, yesterday, and I believe he discussed and asked you about payments and monies. The document reads: The Republic of Serbia, Ministry of Defence. The date is the 1st of November, 1991. It was signed for General Simovic by, as far as I can remember, Mr. Kuzmanovic. You recognise his signature. And now I would like to ask for page 6 of the annex, the attachment, where the manpower levels are mentioned, the number of men, members of the TO of Krajina is shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 6 of this document. That's 65 ter -- if you just bear with me for a moment. ERN number is 2129689 of this attachment that I would like to see. That's page 7, please. Can we enlarge it a bit, please, so that the witness may see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, under 1, operational area Knin, 12.000 men. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operational zone Lika. Let me just have a look. There was no operational zone Knin. There was northern Dalmatia. As for 12.000 men, I don't know who it was that he took into account. Was it the TO units and MUP units?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I apologise. Look at the title. A table of the number of personnel of the SAO Krajina, Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem TO. So we can clearly see that it's TO. So you can see Knin 12.000.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Operational zone Lika, 5.500.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Operational zone Kordun and Banja, 19.000.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this isn't a good count.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that these numbers here are exaggerated. So in your view, what was the number?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 5 to 6.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksic. Please be so kind as to tell us the following: The special unit of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, how many men did it have?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about it. I don't know anything about a special unit. I only heard of one, but I never saw it. I don't know their head count, composition, or location.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Maksic, giving a statement on the 29th and 30th of August? You had an interview with the OTP some five or six days ago, and under item 5 you say special unit of the MUP of Krajina did not have any tasks, nor did it take part in any of the operations. You think that members of this special unit did not have or undergo any special training. Is this what you told Mr. Farr a couple of days back?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation of the special unit of MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. "[In English] The special unit of the Krajina MUP did not have any tasks or engage in any operations."

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall stating this. If I did say this, then I was wrong. I did hear of a special unit existing, but as I say, I never saw it, and I never heard of it carrying out a single task over the three months. I don't recall it ever being engaged within the 9th or 59th Corps. Did it really exist? I don't know. I never saw it, and I never saw its establishment or composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Maksic, you've just explained to us that you didn't know that they were engaged in any sort of operation or whether they existed.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You will recall giving a statement to the OTP in January of 2005; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it happened in February of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, the statement says the 25th and the 26th of January, 2005, Mr. Maksic.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I was there in February of 2004, and if what -- if this is what the document says, then that must be the case. Then I must be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Instead of quarreling about the exact date, I take it that this could be resolved. Read to the witness what you want to put to him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 40 of the statement, you said the special unit of the MUP of SAO Krajina was stationed in Knin and was able to operate throughout the territory of the Krajina. It did not have a firm structure, and it consisted of a group of between 30 and 50 men.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what I read out to you is correct.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you do know that a special unit existed.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they called it a special unit, but it was no special unit. They were not specialists trained in special tasks. That's why I said that it was no special unit of any sort. What I said was that the MUP of Krajina styled it as a special unit, but my claim was that it only had the between 30 to 50 men who were engaged where and as necessary. If needed, men from other police units of the various municipalities would be recruited in order to man this particular special unit, and when they were no longer required they would go back to their original municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, as you stated a couple of days ago, during your stay there you had never heard of this unit ever being engaged in any action of any sort.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, in addition to this unit there existed municipal secretariats of the interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what the manpower levels of the regular police force were?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, was Mr. Babic in command of the TO staff while you were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In formal and legal terms, yes, but in reality, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 2D213. I need the bottom part of it. And this is the start of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: There is a place for the stamp which says -- the round stamp of the SAO Krajina. Dr. Milan Babic signed personally. To the command of the 3rd Operational Zone. In other words, the order issued by the TO staff to relocate 130-millimetre battery and to make them ready to fire upon the target of Zagreb. Are you familiar with this document wherein Milan Babic, the commander of the armed forces, ordered the Territorial Defence, that's to say the command of the 3rd operational area, to fire upon Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 27th -- well, I had already gone by the 27th, and I only returned on the 28th to hand over my duties. So I wasn't in the Krajina at the time. However, at the time, the 9th Corps was still deployed in its area of responsibility. I don't think that anyone resubordinated a rocket system, as is stated here cannons --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: A 130-millimetre battery.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to fire upon Zagreb. Where would Babic have found a 130-millimetre battery if the 9th Corps was still in its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, please have a look. It seems that Babic issues an order to the command of the 3rd operational area.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but whose operational zone is this? I don't think that Babic wrote this. I think somebody wrote it for him. He didn't even sign it. It doesn't have a stamp. There existed two operational areas. One was that of Banja and Kordun, and the other that of Lika and Northern Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, did you not in your earlier statement speak of the existence of three operational areas?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well, there existed three or four operational zones or areas which were then joined. They were transformed. But at the time I was there, there were two operational areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, it is possible that this document is the cause of confusion. In the footnote it says that Milan Babic signed the document himself and that the document bore a round stamp which said "Knin TO staff." Did you have such a round stamp which said "Knin TO staff"?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours can we have this documented admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't this one out of the series that should be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, MFI'd. Madam Registrar, I think we got stuck at D1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not decide. D104 is admitted into evidence, and then the next document shown and not yet admitted into evidence was?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D105 MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, can you explain to us what were units attached to the staff, what do they mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they are units in service of the staff. They provide for the vehicles, food supplies. They make arrangements for accommodation, and then they also include various speciality unit such as transport unit, communications unit, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksic. We don't have much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter 3967.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, while we're waiting for the document to appear, are you familiar with the name of Milos Pupovac?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant for logistics in the command of the defence for the city of Belgrade. He hails from a village close to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, please look at the stamp in the upper left-hand corner. Does it state there the Serbian Autonomous District of the Krajina, Territorial Defence Staff, and then reference numbers and the date of the 16th of December, and then it says Knin. Is this the stamp belonging to your staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Herein the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia is requested to provide ammunition, various types of vehicles, and you can see what is listed here, materiel assets. It is signed by Colonel Pupovac, and the stamp belonging to your staff is affixed here.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of December --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Milos Pupovac only arrived there on the 27th of December. As I was about to set out from Knin, Milos Pupovac had just arrived. I don't see how he could have signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll the document to the bottom. Can we see the signature and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The stamp is all right, as is the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, can you tell us, do you know -- did you, as a TO staff for the purposes of the units attached to your staff, receive these assets from the ministry of defence of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not receive anything. We were also supposed to formulate Martic's requirements. We also reduced them, and we only received from the Ministry of Defence some 30 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Telephone sets. You told us about it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, you said that you copied Martic's requests. And please pause there. I want to finish my question. The moment you got there and set up the TO staff in Knin, Milan Martic no longer had anything to do with Territorial Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't set up the staff. It was General Djujic who was the commander who set it up. I was just the head of the training department. So we set up the staff, and by that point Mr. Martic was minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And no longer deputy of the TO commander.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He dropped by my office on a couple of occasions, but he never interfered with the work of the staff. The staff comprised the four of us. I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But evidently you did have units attached to your staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we tried to set them up, but we did not have enough manpower.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned manpower, can we look at 2D207, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, one question. Your -- your questions about the signature of Mr. Pupovac, was that a mistake or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. This was due to the facts that Mr. Maksic had his suspicions about the date, but he did confirm Mr. Pupovac's signature and the stamp. I forgot to ask that the document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, it's -- it's on e-court. It's a six-page document. That, of course -- apparently you're dealing only with the first two pages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there is some confusion as to whether the transcript reflects that I did admit into evidence D104, and that's -- ask the witness to look at 2D207. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before the document appears on our screen, I would like to revert back to the earlier document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the units attached to the staff are military police units, sabotage units, et cetera, and you say that these units were never formed?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not a single one of them. We had the total of 20 men who stayed there for 28 hours alone and that only because there was an allowance that was still due to them. Thereupon they left, and we had no resources to make sure that they stayed with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksic. Let us look at 2D207 now. This is another document which is an excerpt from a book. I'm telling you this so that there arises no confusion. And according to this book, Dusan Kasim signed this. Was he a Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We don't see this in B/C/S, 2D207.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see is that in English 285 -- 285 appears at the top of the page. And on the Serbian side we have to move to the next page, I take it. In --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You're right. It's the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now would I like to have back in the English version with 285 on top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like the Serbian version to be enlarged for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this is not exactly, for one reason or another -- English and B/C/S seems to be twinned more or less. The English version is right now, and now we need -- yes. Could the B/C/S version be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, are you able to read this? What we have is again a letter from the TO staff in Knin on the 11th of December, 1991, at the time you were there for Colonel Vukosavljevic. It's an overview of independent units of the TO which are manoeuvre units in character as per Municipal Staffs. The Knin TO Municipal Staff numbers two brigades with 1.328 men each; is this right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is there a reason for you to suspect that Mr. Dusan Kasum, your Chief of Staff would falsify the information, or is it the case perhaps that on this date he was not privy to the number of men in the TO unit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two thousand six hundred and fifty-six. Since he dealt with this business he gathered a list of 2.000 men. Actually, what he did was he made up a list of 2.000 men who did not exist in effect in order to be able to put in a request for assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Look at this, Mr. Maksic, please focus. It says Municipal Staff Knin of Territorial Defence, and it says that it's got 2.000 men -- or, rather, in -- in total. So it's not your staff. It's the staff -- the Municipal Staff of TO Knin.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that Municipal Staff did not have a single company while I was there. And this is during my time is there, is it not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. And your Chief of Staff wrote this to the Ministry of Defence of Serbia. In other words, he was falsifying information.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't true. No, this isn't correct. In the town proper -- or as it -- in relation to towns, it was only in Benkovac that we were able to set up a staff, and it was resubordinated to the 9th Corps. I think that the commander's name was Djurica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that in Knin there did not exist a single TO company?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true for the Municipal Staff in Knin. There we did not have a single unit. So we're not talking about the TO staff. We're talking about the Knin Municipal Staff. They did not have a single TO unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, a moment ago I showed you an overview totaling 37.000 men, and you said that this was an exaggeration. Then you volunteered your estimate as to how many men the TO Krajina had. Can you repeat that number?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how many men there were. I think 5 to 6.000 in all. If both of these zones together, and I found a piece of information --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You said 6 to 7.000. Did you say 5 to 6.000 or 6 to 7.000?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six to 7.000. I don't know exactly. Don't hold me to that, but it didn't have more than what I said. And I'm referring to the TO municipal staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: These 7.000 members of Territorial Defence, who were they subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were municipal staffs of Territorial Defence, and they were subordinated to the president of the municipality concerned. The commander of the TO staff is subordinated to the president of the municipality where he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, the document where the municipality of Petrinja subordinated Arkan to the TO staff was a legitimate one, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my 42-year career, I never came across something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, you just said that a TO staff is under the command of the president of the municipality. What does it mean, that he can issue commands and resubordinate?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but through the TO staff in Krajina. He should have sent Arkan's volunteers to the staff, and he should have asked the TO Krajina staff for their approval of the resubordination of these volunteers. What they did instead was they would subordinate these men without the knowledge of the TO staff. They bypassed it. That was the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did the 9th Corps resubordinate Territorial Defence directly or through your staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The 9th Corps resubordinated Territorial Defence in the area of combat in which it happened to be directly through municipal staffs and not through the Krajina TO staff. To put it simply, the military procedure as envisaged under command and control was not complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this 2D document that we've just looked at be admitted into evidence of -- or, rather, MFI'd, 2D207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first go back for a second to 65 ter 3967, which is the six-pages document where apparently you used the two first pages only. Can we have that document marked for identification so that you check -- check whether that's -- we need the whole of the document or two pages. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I believe that 3967 was admitted yesterday as P961.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we verify that. That seems to be correct, so therefore that leaves no decision to be taken on that. Then the last document that was 2D207, Madam Registrar, could you assign a number for -- so that it's marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm now moving that 2D207 be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's what we just did, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had forgotten to activate my microphone. I said that that's what we just had done. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at document 65 ter 447. This is a document dated the 9th of October, 1991. If you're unable to read it, I shall try -- look at the stamp and at the signature. Do you recognise Dr. Babic's signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Babic's signature, and it is the government of Krajina stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is an order from the 9th of October, 1991. All militia units in the area of the Serbian autonomous region of Krajina shall be in planning and carrying out combat tasks shall be resubordinated to the competent officers, to the competent officer of the Territorial Defence. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It is fuzzy. The way it is typewritten, I'm unable to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. But were you aware of the fact that on the 9th of October, 1991, Dr. Milan Babic issued an order resubordinating militia police units in the area of the Serbian autonomous region of Krajina to the commanders of the Territorial Defence of the municipal organs, that is?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of this order, of the existence of this order, and apart from that it could not have been executed according to the law.
